name: Someswarar Temple, Pazhayarai Vadathali
deity: Shiva as Someswarar, with the goddess Somakamalambikai (Somakalambikai)
period: Tevaram era (hymned 7th–8th century); Chola capital, 8th–9th century structural temple
summary: At Pazhayarai Vadathali — once a capital of the early Cholas, near Patteeswaram in the Kumbakonam country — Shiva is honoured as Someswarar with the goddess Somakamalambikai. A Paadal Petra Sthalam revered in the Tevaram by Appar, Sambandar and Sundarar, the shrine stands amid the remembered streets of an old royal city of the delta.

sections.history: Pazhayarai, near Patteeswaram in the Kumbakonam tract of Thanjavur district, was a capital of the early Cholas, and its name — 'the old place' — keeps that memory. The Vadathali, the northern shrine, is a Paadal Petra Sthalam, revered in the Tevaram by Appar, Sambandar and Sundarar; it is believed to have been built in the Chola period, between the 8th and 9th centuries. The site holds several shrines; this is the Someswarar temple.
sections.architecture: A Dravidian temple of the old capital, the shrine enshrines Someswarar in the sanctum, with the goddess Somakamalambikai in her own shrine, a Nandi and the parivara devatas about the prakara. Pazhayarai Vadathali is one of the cluster of shrines — Vadathali, Then-thali and others — that marked the four quarters of the Chola city; the neighbouring Vadathali Dharmapureeswarar shrine, with its goddess Vimalai Nayaki, stands nearby, and sources at times fold the two names together.
sections.legends: Shiva is worshipped here as Someswarar, 'the lord of Soma,' with the goddess Somakamalambikai beside him. The chola kings held Pazhayarai as their seat, and the temples of its quarters carried the devotion of the court; the Vadathali is remembered among the shrines the three samayacharyas — Appar, Sambandar and Sundarar — honoured in their hymns. As with the shrines of the old capital, much of the sthala tradition is bound up with the memory of the Chola city itself.
sections.festivals: The temple observes Maha Shivaratri in Masi (February–March), Navaratri in Purattasi (September–October) and the Mondays of Karthikai, with Pradosha worship. Pilgrims on the Kumbakonam–Patteeswaram circuit of the Paadal Petra temples include Pazhayarai Vadathali, the shrine of the old Chola capital, among their stops.
sections.experience: At Pazhayarai the pilgrim walks the ground of a vanished capital. Before Someswarar and Somakamalambikai, where the streets of an old royal city once ran, the visitor finds the quiet grace of a Tevaram temple honoured by all three samayacharyas — and, in the name 'the old place,' the long memory of the Cholas who ruled from here.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Pazhayarai Vadathali lies near Patteeswaram, about 8 km from Kumbakonam, in Thanjavur district. Kumbakonam is the nearest town and rail head, with buses and taxis to Patteeswaram and Pazhayarai.
